title: WORKSPACE.md frontmatter — agentworkspace/v2 (workspace tree node — THE canonical AIP-34 schema; supersedes v1 outright)
description: Validates the YAML frontmatter portion of an AIP-34 WORKSPACE.md manifest — the canonical workspace/v2 tree-node shape: node `type` (resolved against a sibling TYPES.md), `wall` (visibility level), `includes`/`exports` (two-sided consent doors), `agents`/`routines` (declared manifests this node hosts), `secrets`/`uses_secrets` (never-inherited secret grants), `apps`/`accepted_apps` (versioned app attachments with two-sided consent), `work` (AIP-20 status/board), and `policy.limits` budget aggregation. Supersedes the original workspace/v1 identity-only draft outright — there is no parallel v1 schema; see AIP-34 §Migrating from workspace/v1.

id.description: Globally addressable, FLAT id `@<owner-slug>/<workspace-slug>`. Immutable even if the node moves to a different folder (`ws mv` rewrites the path, never the id).

type.description: Node kind. MUST be a key declared in the nearest ancestor TYPES.md (walking up through folders with no WORKSPACE.md). Day-1 vocabulary: root | perso | company | project | initiative. Hosts/trees MAY register more under TYPES.md; this field stays an open string so the registry — not this schema — is the extension point.

status.description: active: runs normally. paused: keeps declarations/data but runs nothing — hosts MUST NOT start agents or fire routines at or below this node, excluded from budget/heartbeat checks like archived, stays writable and resumes by flipping back to active. archived: read-only, excluded from budget/heartbeat checks, never runs anything. A node's EFFECTIVE status is the most restrictive value along its ancestor chain (archived > paused > active) — a child is never more active than an ancestor; the field itself always holds only this node's own declared value.

work.description: AIP-20 WORK.md block. Optional — when present, this node's status/board is tracked there (items are AIP-18 ITEM.md records under the collection(s) WORK.md declares), not in a flat status file. Same inline/ref/file union shape as `code`.

presence.description: PRESENCE.md block (workspace.presence/v1, see AIP-34 §Presence block). Optional. How this node speaks in public: audience, topics, forbidden words, channels, cadence, approval. Same inline/ref/file union as `work`; a `file` is path-confined.

wall.description: Visibility level toward sibling/ancestor nodes. shared: siblings read the whole node (implicit export `to: "children"` of the PARENT). isolated (default): nothing crosses without an explicit includes/exports door; ancestors still see everything. sealed: as isolated, PLUS ancestors see only this node's EXPORT.md, never raw files; inbound includes require host-side approval (AIP-7). hard: as sealed, PLUS enforced by a separate process/identity — no shared daemon, no shared auth profile, no shared MCP surface; the only traffic in or out is the declared exports, delivered by message, never by mount. A child MAY raise its own wall (shared→isolated→sealed→hard) but MUST NOT set a level looser than its parent's or its TYPES.md entry's `default_wall`.

secrets.description: Ref to this node's OWN .secrets/SECRETS.md inventory (AIP-19). Never inherited — a node with no `secrets` block has no secrets of its own, full stop.

uses_secrets.description: Consumer-side declaration of a secret grant this node expects. Only effective if the named provider workspace's SECRETS.md carries a matching `access.bind[].workspace` (or `.reveal[].workspace`) grant for this node's id — consent MUST exist on both sides, same rule as includes/exports.

accepted_apps.description: Provider-side consent for an `apps[].attach` pointed at THIS node by another node — same two-sided-consent shape as `exports`/`uses_secrets`. An attach with no matching entry here is a conformance error, never silently honoured.

lock.description: Workspace-relative path to this node's apps/packs lockfile (see AIP-34 §agentproto.lock). Only meaningful on nodes that install apps/packs directly; a node that attaches nothing MAY omit it.

safeRelativePath.description: Path confinement (see §Path confinement): tree-relative (no leading `/`), no `..` path segment anywhere. Schema-level best effort — hosts MUST ALSO realpath-resolve and verify containment to catch a symlink escape the string alone can't reveal.

from.description: Id of the workspace whose `apps[].attach` this grant honours.

app.description: Restrict the grant to one app id. Omitted = any app `from` attaches.

share.description: Other workspace ids this agent is also declared transverse to (AIP-34 §Specification (workspace/v2) exception 3). The agent always runs scoped to whichever of these ids is the live caller — never a union of several at once.

ref.description: AIP-54 ws:// ref: `ws://workspaces/<provider-id>[#<subpath>]`. No subpath = the whole node. The `#<subpath>` fragment is path confinement scope (see §Path confinement): no `..` anywhere in it.

path.description: Path (relative to this node) made available to the grantee(s). Path confinement applies — see §Path confinement.

oneOf.description: Sentinel: every node nested, in the folder tree, under whichever workspace DECLARES this export entry — regardless of id. For an explicit entry, that's whoever wrote it. For the IMPLICIT grant `wall: shared` synthesizes, the declaring node is the PARENT, not the shared node itself — so the grant reaches the shared node's SIBLINGS (the parent's other children), not merely its own descendants. See AIP-34 §The four wall levels.
A single named workspace id — the explicit two-sided door case.

from.description: Id of the workspace whose SECRETS.md owns this slug.

version.description: Semver or semver-range (`^0.1.0`, `~1.2.0`, `1.2.3`). Resolved against the installed app store at attach time; the resolved exact version is what lands in agentproto.lock.

attach.description: `"self"` (default): this node and its subtree — no consent needed, the declaring node can only ever restrict itself. Otherwise a workspace id the app is attached to instead — effective ONLY if that target node's WORKSPACE.md declares a matching `accepted_apps` entry granting this node (and optionally this app id); see §Apps and consent. An unconsented cross-node attach is a conformance error, not a silent no-op.

identityRefBlock.description: AIP-23 identity-ref. Single entry or multi-attribution array. Left permissive here; AIP-23 owns the normative shape.

kind.description: AIP-38 limit kind. Budget kinds added by AIP-34 v2: budget-usd-per-month | budget-usd-per-day. Also any AIP-38 kind (max-concurrent-sessions, rate-tool-calls, ...).
